Let \(m=|\mathcal B|\). For a point \(x\in V\), let \(r_x\) be the number of blocks containing \(x\). By hypothesis, every \(r_x\) is even.

Fix \(x\). Each block containing \(x\) has the form
\[
\{x,a,b,c\},
\]
so it determines a triple \(\{a,b,c\}\) in the other \(10\) points. Since no \(3\)-subset of \(V\) lies in two blocks, no pair \(\{a,b\}\) among those other \(10\) points can occur in two of these triples. Thus the \(r_x\) triples form a packing of edge-disjoint triangles in \(K_{10}\).

Such a packing has at most \(13\) triangles. Indeed, \(15\) triangles would decompose all \(45\) edges of \(K_{10}\), impossible because each vertex degree \(9\) would have to be even in a triangle decomposition. Also \(14\) triangles would leave \(45-42=3\) edges; but then every vertex would have odd leftover degree, since \(9-2d\) is odd, requiring at least \(10\) odd-degree vertices, impossible with only \(3\) edges.

So \(r_x\le 13\). Since \(r_x\) is even, actually
\[
r_x\le 12.
\]
Therefore
\[
4m=\sum_{x\in V} r_x \le 11\cdot 12=132,
\]
so
\[
m\le 33.
\]

It remains to show \(33\) is attainable. Identify \(V\) with \(\mathbb Z/11\mathbb Z\). Take all cyclic translates of the following three blocks:
\[
\{0,1,2,4\},\qquad \{0,1,5,8\},\qquad \{0,2,5,7\}.
\]
This gives \(3\cdot 11=33\) blocks. Each point appears \(4\) times in each orbit, hence \(12\) times total, which is even.

The no-repeated-triple condition holds because the \(12\) triples inside the three base blocks have distinct cyclic gap types:
\[
(1,1,9),(1,2,8),(1,3,7),(2,2,7),
\]
\[
(1,4,6),(1,7,3),(3,3,5),(3,4,4),
\]
\[
(2,3,6),(2,5,4),(2,4,5),(2,6,3).
\]
Thus no translate of one contained triple equals another contained triple.

Hence the maximum possible value is
\[
\boxed{33}.
\]
